title: AI VHS Effect Generator
summary: Make a VHS effect with AI. Describe the year and the tape damage, and Flick makes the clip, or restyle your own video with a VHS filter look.
body_markdown:
### What does a VHS filter do?


A VHS filter imitates the limits of analog videotape: soft detail, colours that bleed past their edges, horizontal noise and an unsteady picture. Many filters also add an on-screen date or PLAY text like an old camcorder.


### Can I get a VHS effect for free?


Yes, you can start free: you get 100 credits when you sign up, 200 more for joining the Flick Discord, and 100 credits every week. The clips on this page used GPT Image 2.5 and MiniMax H3 Fast, which both run on the free plan, and downloads carry a Flick watermark.


### Can I add a VHS effect to my own video?


Yes. Upload the clip to a Flick canvas and use Edit Video with a prompt describing the tape damage you want. A simple overlay filter in a video editor is another option if you want the footage itself left unchanged.


### What is the difference between a VHS filter and a VHS effect?


The two terms are mostly used for the same look. A filter usually means a preset applied to existing video, while an effect can also mean overlays, sound or damage built into the shot itself.


### How do I make found footage look real?


Use a single light source on the camera, heavy grain and an on-screen REC stamp, then keep the camera moving slowly by hand. Letting tape noise hide part of the action does more for the fear than showing it clearly.
